title: Increasing the Potential of Liquid Cell TEM Through the Accumulation of Small Improvements
content: In order to observe various phenomena occurring in liquids at the nanoscale in-situ, we have been gradually improving liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LC-TEM) by developing software and hardware in addition to establishing sample preparation and observation methods. In terms of software, in addition to image improvement using machine learning [1], we are also investigating particle detection [2] and developing an embryo detection model for the nucleation of nanoparticles from a solution [3]. In particular, the embryo detection model attempts to understand the pre-nucleation phenomenon by capturing the contrast fluctuations before particles nucleate from the solution. In terms of hardware, we are developing a chip by micro electro mechanical systems (MEMS) to trap particles by dielectrophoresis [4] and a Peltier cooling holder to enable in-situ observation of the phase transition between water and ice [5]. In addition, in terms of observation methods, we have explored conditions for containing relatively large volumes of solution using a graphene liquid cell [6] and established a method for observing the collapse process of the microstructure of semiconductor surfaces after washing and drying [7] .
